assessment.rationale: Useful as a narrow CAS/app-boundary input, but mostly off-target for this porting scenario: it clarifies provisional blob-contract limits yet does not define the porting surface, terminology, harness separation, or first-port conformance claim.
strengths: Explicitly keeps replication, retention, discovery, ingress, and hash-as-capability outside any overclaimed base CAS guarantee.
Strong draft-vs-frozen-spec caution and explicit acknowledgement of open DRs.
Frames 100-year survival and non-canonical implementation choice as design constraints.
weaknesses: Does not say what the minimum viable porting target is before freeze.
Does not separate wire-lab harness apparatus from real host-port obligations.
Does not cover runtime/kernel/dispatcher/library terminology or binding/session/message/feed conformance scope.
risks: Readers could misread app-level blob guidance as kernel or runtime porting guidance.
A provisional CAS profile could be treated as a premature conformance obligation.
Missing non-CAS layer boundaries may create a false sense that a first port is more specified than it is.
open_questions: What terminology should the guide standardize on for the porting target before DR-davod closes?
Which K1-K5 ingress, feed, session, message, and app-layer details are blocked versus provisionally portable?
Can any CAS-facing draft profile be part of a first-port claim, or should it stay app-orientation only until freeze?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
